description:
Plan is a multi-step DAG that decomposes into owner-ref'd AgentRun CRs.

The Go plan reconciler is ALWAYS active — it reconciles every Plan on every
cluster. (The former LEARTECH_PLAN_RECONCILER_ENABLED enable-gate has been
removed now that the Go reconciler is authoritative.)

apiVersion.description:
APIVersion defines the versioned schema of this representation of an object.
Servers should convert recognized schemas to the latest internal value, and
may reject unrecognized values.
More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#resources

kind.description:
Kind is a string value representing the REST resource this object represents.
Servers may infer this from the endpoint the client submits requests to.
Cannot be updated.
In CamelCase.
More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#types-kinds

spec.description:
PlanSpec is the desired state of a Plan (a multi-step DAG of AgentRuns).

The Plan reconciler decomposes the Spec into owner-ref'd AgentRun CRs,
creating each step only after every DependsOn step reaches Succeeded. This
is the Go replacement for orch's Python plan_runner — SHADOW/GATED in this
slice (see cmd/server/main.go), orch remains authoritative until cut-over.

command.description:
Command is the pending control-surface command. The reconciler
consumes it exactly-once (idempotent via
Status.LastAcknowledgedCommandUID) and translates the verb into
declarative status transitions (see PlanCommandVerb).

reason.description:
Reason is a free-form annotation persisted onto the audit log entry
(Plan.Status.Decisions[]) when the command is consumed. Used by the
re-plan agent to record its rationale.

uid.description:
UID uniquely identifies this command emission. Idempotency key —
two reconciles of the same UID must produce identical status. Callers
generate this (ULID / UUID / monotonic counter).

verb.description: Verb is one of pause | resume | cancel | replan.

paused.description:
Paused is the plan-level HALT gate. When true, the reconciler MUST
NOT spawn any AgentRun on this reconcile, regardless of step
readiness. Set by an external actor (agent, kubectl edit) as the
re-plan safety gate. Clearing Paused=false lets normal reconciliation
resume from the current state.

remediates.description:
Remediates lists Plan references this Plan is designed to remediate.
When THIS Plan reaches PlanPhaseSucceeded (and its final verification
step succeeded), each referenced plan's Status.Phase is flipped to
PlanPhaseResolved and its Status.ResolvedBy is set to a PlanRef for
THIS plan. One remediation may resolve MANY referenced plans in a
single reconcile pass — the fan-out is atomic-per-referenced-plan
(individual referenced-plan updates are logged + skipped on error;
the next reconcile retries the remaining).

A Plan with Remediates set that itself Fails / Cancels does NOT
resolve its referenced plans — resolution is gated on the
remediating plan's OWN success. The referenced plans retain their
terminal Failed / Cancelled phase, honestly reflecting that no
remediation landed.

Loop-guard: a remediation plan is subject to signature-based dedupe
(agent.leartech.io/remediation-signature annotation) and a depth cap
(RemediationMaxDepth) enforced at admission — see
PlanReconciler.enforceRemediationLoopGuard. A duplicate remediation
(same signature as an earlier sibling) OR a chain exceeding the cap
is terminated as Cancelled with an audit-log entry before any step
spawns; the guard is deliberately LOUD (structured log + decision)
rather than silent-drop.

items.description:
PlanRef references another Plan by name + optional namespace. Used by
Plan.Spec.Remediates (the list of plans a remediation targets) and
Plan.Status.ResolvedBy (the back-link on a Resolved plan naming the
remediating plan). Kept small + opaque — the controller resolves the
pair to a live Plan CR via a namespaced Get.

Empty Namespace defaults to the referencing plan's own namespace at
resolve-time. Cross-namespace references are permitted (a cluster-wide
remediation plan can reference plans in per-tenant namespaces) but the
referencing plan's ServiceAccount must have get/patch on plans in the
target namespace for the resolution to succeed.

name.description: Name is the referenced Plan.metadata.name. Required.

namespace.description:
Namespace is the referenced Plan.metadata.namespace. Optional —
empty defaults to the referencing plan's own namespace.

steps.description: Steps declares the DAG. Each step Name must be unique.

items.description:
PlanStep declares one node in the plan DAG. Each step maps 1:1 to an
AgentRun the reconciler will create when the step's DependsOn are all
Succeeded (or empty). Step Names must be unique within the Plan and stable
(they're used to compute the deterministic AgentRun name — see
PlanReconciler.agentRunName).

agentType.description:
AgentType names the cluster-scoped AgentType CR the step's AgentRun runs
on (per-language runtime — mirrors AgentRunSpec.AgentType). Optional:
when empty the controller falls back to the configured default
(LEARTECH_DEFAULT_AGENT_TYPE). The BA/Planner normally sets it
explicitly per repo language (the policy path).

budgetIter.description:
BudgetIter caps AgentRun iterations for this step. When nil, the
AgentType default applies (mirrors AgentRunSpec.BudgetIter).

dependsOn.description:
DependsOn lists step Names this step waits on. Empty = ready at t=0.
Cycles are rejected at reconcile time (the DAG walker halts + fails).

A step is eligible only when every DependsOn step is *Succeeded*.
A Failed OR Cancelled dependency keeps the dependent BLOCKED
(Cancelled != success). See PlanReconciler.depsReady.

fanIn.description:
FanIn marks the step as a fan-in validation step: a NO-AGENT,
read-only check that asserts every file listed in FanInValidate
exists on the repo's main HEAD before the step's dependents may
proceed. A fan-in step does NOT spawn an AgentRun — the reconciler
resolves the repo's main HEAD sha and probes each expected file on
that ref via the wired FanInValidator seam.

Semantics:
  - All expected files present → step advances to StepPhaseSucceeded
    (validation passed) → dependents unblock on the next reconcile.
  - Any expected file missing → step advances to StepPhaseFailed
    (block dependents; the missing paths are surfaced in a
    "fan_in_failed" decision entry).

A fan-in step MUST declare ≥1 DependsOn (a step with no upstream
producers has nothing to validate) AND ≥1 FanInValidate path. A
non-fan-in step MUST NOT declare FanInValidate. The DAG validator
terminally fails the Plan on either misuse.

Mirrors orch's Python plan_runner execute_fan_in_step /
_resolve_main_head_sha / _file_exists_on_ref path.

fanInValidate.description:
FanInValidate lists repo-relative file paths that MUST exist on the
repo's main HEAD for the fan-in step to succeed. Ignored when FanIn
is false; required (non-empty) when FanIn is true. Paths are opaque
to the reconciler — the FanInValidator seam owns the "does this path
exist on that ref?" answer.

hold.description:
Hold, when true, marks the step's PR deliberately held pending human
approval. The plan authors this bit — it tells downstream consumers
"this step's PR is meant to be reviewed by a human, not auto-merged
by Tide once gates go green". The reconciler routes such a step to
StepPhaseAwaitingApproval (distinct from AwaitingReview) once its
agent finishes AND opens a PR — so chat/UX can say "waiting on human
approval" rather than the generic "PR is being reviewed / gates
still running".

The two are semantically different:

  - AwaitingReview (Hold=false): transient. Gates + AI review may
    still be running; Tide will merge as soon as the PR is green,
    which advances the step to Succeeded on the next reconcile.
  - AwaitingApproval (Hold=true): parked. The agent posted /hold to
    Lighthouse Keeper; Tide will NOT merge until a human explicitly
    posts /hold cancel. The step sits here indefinitely.

Both keep dependents blocked (both are non-terminal for depsReady
purposes). Hold does NOT change how depsReady/rollUp key off
StepPhaseSucceeded (still requires PR merged).

The AgentRun-level Phase stays Succeeded for a held step — the
agent finished; it is the DELIVERABLE that is parked, not the run.

inputs.description:
Inputs is the run payload projected into the AgentRun (mirrors
AgentRunSpec.Inputs — validated by the AgentType's InputSchema).
Optional: a `use:` step MUST NOT declare inputs (they come from the
expanded template steps), so inputs cannot be schema-required or a
Template-Plan composition is unconstructible via the API. Non-use
steps normally set it; the expander/agent handle an empty payload.

kind.description:
Kind declares HOW the reconciler judges this step "done" — a
first-class dimension distinct from the step's phase. Three kinds,
each with its own done-semantics (see PlanReconciler.deriveStepPhase):

	""  ≡ "pr" (default; back-compat — an empty Kind is a pr step).
	"pr"    → the step's deliverable is a PULL REQUEST; the step is done
	          when that PR MERGES. AgentRun Succeeded + PR merged →
	          StepPhaseSucceeded; PR closed-unmerged → StepPhaseFailed; a
	          repo-backed run that finished with no PR after the report-back
	          grace → StepPhaseFailed ("no deliverable"). This is the
	          historical merge-gated behaviour, unchanged.
	"apply" → idempotent / DIRECT work with NO PR expected (registration,
	          to_main pushes, cluster mutations). The step is done when the
	          AgentRun SUCCEEDS (exit 0) — Succeeded → StepPhaseSucceeded
	          with NO PR required (the no-PR "no-deliverable" fail is NEVER
	          applied). Failed → StepPhaseFailed; Cancelled → Cancelled.
	"check" → a VERIFICATION step judged by a DETERMINISTIC, framework-
	          owned verdict (NOT an LLM narration): AgentRun Succeeded →
	          verdict PASS → StepPhaseSucceeded; AgentRun Failed → verdict
	          FAIL → StepPhaseFailed. Any PR the run opens is IGNORED for
	          the pass/fail decision. The controller writes the verdict to
	          PlanStepStatus.Verdict.

An unrecognised Kind is treated as "pr" (the safe default). Kind does
not change DAG gating — depsReady/rollUp still key off StepPhaseSucceeded
regardless of kind.

name.description:
Name uniquely identifies the step within this Plan. Used to compute the
child AgentRun's name (<plan>-<step>), so must be a valid DNS-1123 label
component (kubebuilder validation enforces this at the CRD schema level).

repo.description: Repo, when set, is passed to the AgentRun (git clone init-container).

test.description:
Test, when set on a step whose Plan is a test Plan (PlanSpec.Test),
declares the DIRECTED outcome the machinery should simulate for this
step INSTEAD OF spawning a real agent Job. It is the per-step half of
the Plan-level test declaration: PlanSpec.Test marks the whole Plan a
test; PlanStep.Test tells the reconciler how THIS step's synthetic PR
"resolves" (merged / closed / opened).

The reconciler consumes this only when the owning Plan is a test Plan:
at child-AgentRun creation it stamps the child with the test-mode
label + the directed-PR-outcome annotation derived from Test.Directed,
so the existing TestModePROutcomeFetcher resolves the outcome at
RUNTIME (not merely in unit tests). See PlanStepTest.Directed.

Ignored when PlanSpec.Test is false — a production Plan never simulates
outcomes even if a step carries a stray Test directive.

directed.description:
Directed names the outcome the machinery should simulate for this step.
The accepted vocabulary is KIND-SPECIFIC (see PlanStep.Kind) — the
controller maps (kind, directed) → the AgentRun terminal phase [+ a
synthetic PR outcome for pr steps] so the SAME step state machine
resolves the step exactly as a real run would:

	kind: pr | "" (merge-gated, the historical vocabulary):
	  "merged"          → PR merged → step Succeeded.
	  "closed_unmerged" → PR closed without merging → step Failed.
	  "opened"          → PR open, not yet merged → step AwaitingReview
	                      (AwaitingApproval when Hold=true).

	kind: check (deterministic verdict):
	  "pass" → AgentRun Succeeded → verdict PASS → step Succeeded.
	  "fail" → AgentRun Failed    → verdict FAIL → step Failed.

	kind: apply (run-success, no PR):
	  "succeed" → AgentRun Succeeded → step Succeeded (no PR expected).
	  "error"   → AgentRun Failed    → step Failed.

An empty or unrecognised Directed leaves the step at its default
simulated outcome (the agent "Succeeded" with no directed result),
which collapses to StepPhaseSucceeded for a repo-less pr step, an apply
step, or a check step (verdict PASS).

triggeredWhen.description:
TriggeredWhen, when set, spawns this step as soon as the named step
REACHES the given step phase (or a later success phase) — a runtime
handoff distinct from DependsOn's "wait for merged/Succeeded". The
motivating case: a Dev step opens its PR (StepPhaseAwaitingReview) and
an Infra "release-monitor" step should fire immediately to watch it
through review → merge → release → health, rather than waiting for the
Dev step to reach Succeeded.

Semantics ("reached-or-beyond", success-path only):
  - Satisfied when the target's step phase rank >= TriggeredWhen.Phase's
    rank on the success ladder Pending<Running<AwaitingReview≈
    AwaitingApproval<Succeeded. So TriggeredWhen{Phase: AwaitingReview}
    fires on AwaitingReview, AwaitingApproval, OR a fast Succeeded — no
    missed transition.
  - A target at Failed/Cancelled NEVER satisfies it (the triggered step
    stays unspawned); the Plan still rolls up to Failed via the target,
    so nothing hangs.
  - Evaluated ALONGSIDE DependsOn: a step with both spawns only when
    (all DependsOn Succeeded) AND (TriggeredWhen reached). A step with
    only TriggeredWhen fires purely on the trigger.

phase.description:
Phase is the step phase that (once reached, or surpassed on the success
ladder) spawns the owning step.

step.description: Step is the name of the step to watch (must be a declared step in the Plan).

use.description:
Use, when set, marks this step as a TEMPLATE-EXPANSION step: a named
PlanTemplate is fetched at plan init, its Steps are substituted with
this step's With params, namespaced under this step's Name (as
"<Name>-<tmplStep>"), and INLINED into the plan's DAG. The
use-step's own DependsOn become the DependsOn of the template's ENTRY
step(s); anything else in the plan that DependsOn THIS step is
rewired to DependsOn the template's TERMINAL step(s) (multi-terminal
= fan-in). The expansion is a pure pre-process — the template's
steps run as normal flat-DAG steps; a controller does NOT spawn
another controller.

A step with Use set MUST NOT declare AgentType / Inputs / Repo /
BudgetIter / Hold / FanIn / FanInValidate / TriggeredWhen; only
DependsOn (external entry-wiring) is honoured. The AgentType +
Inputs come from the expanded template steps themselves.

See PlanTemplate for the referenced type and the expansion semantics
(~/leartech/Hub/status/plan-templates-and-triggers.md).

with.description:
With supplies param values for the PlanTemplate referenced by Use.
The expander substitutes "${name}" occurrences in template step
fields (Name, AgentType, Repo, DependsOn entries) and in the raw
JSON of each template step's Inputs with the provided value.

A template param declared Required=true whose Name has no With
entry is a terminal expansion error (the Plan is marked Failed,
not a panic). An optional param without a With entry substitutes
to the empty string.

tenant.description: Tenant is the tenant identity carried into each child AgentRun.

test.description:
Test marks the whole Plan a TEST Plan. When true, the reconciler runs
the plan's DAG in MACHINERY test-mode: at each step's child-AgentRun
creation it stamps the child with the test-mode label + the directed
PR-outcome annotation derived from the step's Test.Directed, and the
AgentRun reconciler SKIPS spawning a real Job — it terminalizes the
run (Phase=Succeeded) so the directed PR outcome (via the
TestModePROutcomeFetcher wrapper + deriveStepPhase) decides the STEP's
pass/fail. This exercises the full plan/step state machine — DAG walk,
dep-gating, roll-up, merge-gating — WITHOUT running any agent, so a
committed scenario-Plan library can assert reconciler behaviour
deterministically (see test/scenarios/).

A test Plan is otherwise an ordinary Plan: pause/resume/cancel,
fan-in, template expansion, remediation all behave identically. Only
the agent-spawn is machinery-simulated. Production Plans leave this
false and never simulate outcomes.

status.description: PlanStatus is the observed state of a Plan.

completionTime.description: CompletionTime is when the Plan reached a terminal phase.

conditions.description:
Conditions record the plan-level state facts: Paused, Cancelled,
CommandAcknowledged. Standard metav1.Condition shape so kubectl +
dashboards render them natively.

items.description: Condition contains details for one aspect of the current state of this API Resource.

lastTransitionTime.description:
lastTransitionTime is the last time the condition transitioned from one status to another.
This should be when the underlying condition changed.  If that is not known, then using the time when the API field changed is acceptable.

message.description:
message is a human readable message indicating details about the transition.
This may be an empty string.

observedGeneration.description:
observedGeneration represents the .metadata.generation that the condition was set based upon.
For instance, if .metadata.generation is currently 12, but the .status.conditions[x].observedGeneration is 9, the condition is out of date
with respect to the current state of the instance.

reason.description:
reason contains a programmatic identifier indicating the reason for the condition's last transition.
Producers of specific condition types may define expected values and meanings for this field,
and whether the values are considered a guaranteed API.
The value should be a CamelCase string.
This field may not be empty.

status.description: status of the condition, one of True, False, Unknown.

type.description: type of condition in CamelCase or in foo.example.com/CamelCase.

decisions.description:
Decisions is the append-only audit log of transitions the reconciler
applied. Bounded at PlanDecisionsMax entries; oldest-first drop on
overflow. Reproduces the key rows of orch's Python plan_runner
plan_decisions table locally on the CR so the re-plan agent can read
the audit without a database round-trip.

items.description:
PlanDecision is one entry in the append-only audit log of transitions the
reconciler applied to the Plan. Reproduces the load-bearing rows of the
Python plan_runner's plan_decisions table so resume + idempotency logic can
read the same audit locally on the CR.

The log is bounded — the reconciler caps Status.Decisions at
PlanDecisionsMax entries, dropping oldest-first on overflow. Consumers must
not rely on the log being complete over long horizons; for durable audit
use the Maestro plan.* event stream.

message.description: Message is a human-readable detail (mirrors metav1.Condition.Message).

reason.description: Reason is a short machine-readable rationale (mirrors metav1.Condition.Reason).

step.description: Step is the PlanStep.Name involved, when the type is step-*.

time.description: Time is when the transition was applied (reconciler clock).

type.description:
Type identifies the transition:
  paused | resumed | cancelled | replan
  step-fired | step-terminal

expandedSteps.description:
ExpandedSteps is the frozen, post-template-expansion snapshot of the
plan's DAG. Populated once at plan init when any Spec.Steps entry
declares Use (PlanTemplate reference); left empty otherwise. Once set
it is authoritative — every downstream reconcile pass (depsReady,
spawn, roll-up, roll-up fan-in / anti-stomp) walks the SNAPSHOT rather
than Spec.Steps.

This freeze is deliberate: a mid-run template edit MUST NOT mutate an
already-running plan (the same idempotency contract as spec.Steps —
callers edit spec + resume; they don't mutate templates and expect
running plans to pick up the change).

A plan with no Use references leaves ExpandedSteps nil forever; the
reconciler transparently walks Spec.Steps in that case (the effective-
steps helper folds the two paths). See PlanReconciler.expandTemplates.

    rank on the success ladder Pending<Running<AwaitingReview≈
    AwaitingApproval<Succeeded. So TriggeredWhen{Phase: AwaitingReview}
    fires on AwaitingReview, AwaitingApproval, OR a fast Succeeded — no
    missed transition.
  - A target at Failed/Cancelled NEVER satisfies it (the triggered step
    stays unspawned); the Plan still rolls up to Failed via the target,
    so nothing hangs.
  - Evaluated ALONGSIDE DependsOn: a step with both spawns only when
    (all DependsOn Succeeded) AND (TriggeredWhen reached). A step with
    only TriggeredWhen fires purely on the trigger.

phase.description:
Phase is the step phase that (once reached, or surpassed on the success
ladder) spawns the owning step.

step.description: Step is the name of the step to watch (must be a declared step in the Plan).

use.description:
Use, when set, marks this step as a TEMPLATE-EXPANSION step: a named
PlanTemplate is fetched at plan init, its Steps are substituted with
this step's With params, namespaced under this step's Name (as
"<Name>-<tmplStep>"), and INLINED into the plan's DAG. The
use-step's own DependsOn become the DependsOn of the template's ENTRY
step(s); anything else in the plan that DependsOn THIS step is
rewired to DependsOn the template's TERMINAL step(s) (multi-terminal
= fan-in). The expansion is a pure pre-process — the template's
steps run as normal flat-DAG steps; a controller does NOT spawn
another controller.

A step with Use set MUST NOT declare AgentType / Inputs / Repo /
BudgetIter / Hold / FanIn / FanInValidate / TriggeredWhen; only
DependsOn (external entry-wiring) is honoured. The AgentType +
Inputs come from the expanded template steps themselves.

See PlanTemplate for the referenced type and the expansion semantics
(~/leartech/Hub/status/plan-templates-and-triggers.md).

with.description:
With supplies param values for the PlanTemplate referenced by Use.
The expander substitutes "${name}" occurrences in template step
fields (Name, AgentType, Repo, DependsOn entries) and in the raw
JSON of each template step's Inputs with the provided value.

A template param declared Required=true whose Name has no With
entry is a terminal expansion error (the Plan is marked Failed,
not a panic). An optional param without a With entry substitutes
to the empty string.

lastAcknowledgedCommandUID.description:
LastAcknowledgedCommandUID is the UID of the most-recently consumed
PlanSpec.Command. Idempotency key — the reconciler skips re-applying
a command whose UID already appears here.

message.description: Message is a human-readable status detail (e.g. cycle-detected).

observedGeneration.description: ObservedGeneration is the .metadata.generation the status reflects.

phase.description: Phase is the rolled-up lifecycle phase (see PlanReconciler.rollUp).

resolvedBy.description:
ResolvedBy is the back-link set when a SEPARATE remediation plan
flipped this plan's Phase to PlanPhaseResolved — see PlanPhaseResolved
godoc for the semantics. Nil for any non-Resolved plan.

Populated by PlanReconciler.processRemediationResolution when a
remediating plan (whose Spec.Remediates references THIS plan) reaches
Succeeded. The back-link is a name+namespace pair (not a UID) so a
re-created / GC'd remediating plan doesn't dangle the ref — consumers
treat a missing target as "the remediation was archived; the marker
stands".

Idempotency: the reconciler NEVER overwrites an existing ResolvedBy —
the first remediation to resolve this plan wins. A second remediation
referencing the same already-Resolved plan is a no-op (see
processRemediationResolution).

name.description: Name is the referenced Plan.metadata.name. Required.

namespace.description:
Namespace is the referenced Plan.metadata.namespace. Optional —
empty defaults to the referencing plan's own namespace.

startTime.description: StartTime is when the first step was spawned.

steps.description: Steps mirrors Spec.Steps with observed phase + child AgentRun name.

items.description:
PlanStepStatus is the observed state of a single step: its rolled-up phase
and the AgentRun name the reconciler created for it (empty until the step
is spawned).

agentRunName.description:
AgentRunName is the deterministic name of the child AgentRun
(<plan>-<step>); empty until the step is spawned.

headBranch.description:
HeadBranch is the source branch the PR was opened from, when known.
Recorded alongside PR so consumers can pull the branch (for local
review, for cross-repo dependency tracking) without an extra GitHub
round-trip. Empty when the AgentRun didn't report a head branch.

message.description:
Message is a short human-readable diagnostic set by the reconciler
when a step transitions to a terminal StepPhase for a
non-obvious reason. Populated for cases like "repo-backed step's
AgentRun Succeeded but no PR was opened" — surfacing the cause on
the step itself so operators + dashboards don't have to cross-
reference the plan-level decision log. Empty for the common case
(Succeeded via merged PR, ordinary Failed via failed AgentRun, ...).

name.description: Name is the PlanSpec.Steps[].Name this status refers to.

phase.description:
Phase mirrors the step's AgentRun.Status.Phase (Pending when not yet
spawned).

When the Plan is Cancelled (via cancel/replan command), any
non-terminal step's Phase is FORCED to Cancelled — the reconciler
overrides the child AgentRun's observed phase because the plan-level
decision takes precedence.

Phase B2 note: this remains the RAW AgentRun phase for backward-compat
signal is StepPhase below, which factors in the PR OUTCOME
(opened/awaiting-review/merged/closed-unmerged) — an agent Succeeded
only means the PR opened, not that its changes landed.

pr.description:
PR is the pull-request number the step's child AgentRun opened, as
reported via AgentRun.Status.TargetPR. Empty until the agent reports
one. Recorded here so consumers (dashboards, the re-plan agent) can
link a step to its PR without re-listing the child AgentRun.

String rather than int because AgentRun.Status.TargetPR is a string
(some callers use "org/repo#123" schemes) — kept opaque to the plan
reconciler.

prOutcome.description:
PROutcome is the last-observed PR outcome from the outcome fetcher.
One of: "opened" | "awaiting_review" | "merged" | "closed_unmerged".
Empty until the reconciler has queried the outcome at least once (or
when no PR was opened for this step). Advances StepPhase per
_OUTCOME_TRANSITIONS (see plan_controller.go).

retryCount.description:
RetryCount is the number of times the reconciler has respawned this
step's AgentRun after detecting the previous one went dead — i.e. it
was recorded on Status.Steps[].AgentRunName but is no longer resident
on the apiserver (deleted, GC'd, or otherwise vanished before a clean
terminal transition). Bounded at PlanStepMaxRetries; once exhausted
the reconciler marks the step StepPhaseFailed with a
"step-dead-runner" audit entry and stops re-spawning it.

Monotonic per step lifetime. A step that spawned cleanly, ran to a
terminal phase, and never lost its AgentRun stays at RetryCount=0.
A step whose AgentRun vanished N times and was respawned each time
records RetryCount=N (until N reaches the cap, at which point the
step is marked Failed instead of retried).

Mirrors orch's Python plan_runner dead_runner_detector + step_retry:
the same bounded-retry semantics ported to the Go reconciler so a
dead runner doesn't leave the plan hanging forever.

stepPhase.description:
StepPhase is the step-level lifecycle phase — the authoritative signal
the reconciler uses for depsReady + Plan roll-up. Distinct from Phase
above because a step's work isn't done until its PR is MERGED, not
merely when the agent finishes (agents hold PRs; they don't merge).

See PlanStepPhase for the value set + StepPhaseAwaitingReview for the
intermediate state between "agent finished" and "PR merged".

verdict.description:
Verdict is the DETERMINISTIC, framework-owned pass/fail judgement for a
kind:check step. One of "" | "PASS" | "FAIL". The AGENT does NOT set
this — the controller DERIVES it from the check step's AgentRun outcome
(AgentRun Succeeded → "PASS" → StepPhaseSucceeded; AgentRun Failed →
"FAIL" → StepPhaseFailed) in deriveStepPhase. Left "" for kind:pr and
kind:apply steps (they are not verdict-judged; their pass/fail comes
from PR-merge / run-success respectively).

This is what makes a check step's outcome trustworthy: the verdict is
mechanical (keyed off the run's exit) rather than parsed from an LLM's
self-report, so a check can't "narrate" itself green.
